chunks: A man asked Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said to him: “O son of the cousin of the best of the creation of Allah, Exalted is He, what is the meaning of raising your hands in the first takbīrah?” So he عليه السلام said:
“Its meaning is: Allah is the Greatest, the One, the Unique, the One who
He is not touched by the limbs, nor perceived by the senses.”

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَةِ الْأُولَى: the first takbīrah, the opening glorification in salat
key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allah is the Greatest; declaration of divine greatness
key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: nothing whatsoever is like Him; affirmation of divine incomparability

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of raising the hands in the first takbīrah of salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that raising the hands in the opening takbīrah signifies affirming Allah’s absolute greatness and tawhid. It also emphasizes His transcendence: Allah cannot be compared to creation, nor grasped by physical touch or sensory perception.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.921 - A man asked The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) saying:
"O’ son of the cousin of the best of Allah’s (swt) creation, what is the meaning of raising your hands in the first Takbir (opening glorification of Allah (swt))?"
He (as) replied:
"It signifies that Allah (swt) is the Greatest, the One, the Unique,
Who 'there is nothing like unto Him.'
He cannot be perceived by the senses nor touched by the limbs."
